messages:
sam: Quick thread — we saw a perf regression after the autotuner flip. Baseline: kernel-selector now picks arch-aware kernels (AVX512 / CUDA-sm75) by seqlen. Our KV cache keys are model_id+session_id+seq_bin. Thinking we need to include kernel/driver info in keying or change persistence/invalidation rules. Observed ~12% p95 latency increase on long-seqlen after warm restart. Anyone else seeing this?

anya: Yup, saw same in staging after yesterday's deploy. Profiler shows a spike in cache misses during the warm-up window — KV hits fell and batching behaved oddly.

mike: We intentionally kept keys minimal to maximize reuse across variants. But if kernel choice changes KV layout (different kv-shapes / packing), reusing old keys is unsafe. Did the regression correlate with a different kernel binary being used?

leo: It did. Canary logs show selector picked a new kernel binary id=kb_2026_031. The kernel's kv serialization changed (we added 2-byte header). Old entries couldn't be read and fell back -> misses.

tess: Two ideas: add a compatibility tag to keying (so compatible kernels can share) OR include kernel_binary_hash to force isolation. Also soft-ttl + background compaction to avoid full flush on minor changes.

mike: Proposed key schema (draft):
```
model:{model_id}:variant:{variant}:kernel_compat:{compat_tag}:seqbin:{seq_bin}:prefix_hash:{phash}
```
compat_tag could be either a kernel_binary_hash (strong) or an abstract tuple (arch, quant, kv_layout_v).

sam: For rolling upgrades we need a handshake: driver/runtime should announce kernel_compat table and whether reads can accept older layouts. Otherwise we risk silent corruption or repeated cache misses.

runtime-bot: deploy 2151234590: kernel-autotune v3 rolled to canary (5% nodes).

anya: Could we persist keys across restarts if the runtime verifies compatibility? e.g., store metadata next to keys: "kv_layout_v" and allow reading if matches. Avoids invalidating entire namespace.

leo: How to compute compat_tag deterministically? Suggestion: (arch, quant_bits, kernel_major, kv_layout_version). kv_layout_version should be bumped when serialization changes. Kernel build should emit this.

tess: FWIW perf numbers from canary: before change p95=210ms on long seq; after canary p95=235ms. Cache miss rate jumped 6% -> 24% for seq>1024 windows. CPU usage on hosts rose ~8%.

mike: Concrete rollout proposal:
1) Augment key space with kernel_compat tag (default to legacy for existing keys)
2) Add metadata next to keys: kv_layout_v and kernel_binary_id
3) Accept reads if kv_layout_v matches; on mismatch mark as incompatible and optionally schedule conversion job
4) Soft migration: for X minutes allow legacy reads but increment a metric and re-encode on write
5) If driver/runtime bump would cause kv_layout change, trigger explicit invalidation flow with graceful TTL decay

sam: Metrics we need to add before rollout: key_cohort_miss_by_compat, kv_incompat_reads, background_conversion_failures, miss_latency_delta. Also add tracing tag from selector: kernel_choice and seq_bin at request.

anya: Also add a guard in the autotuner: if a kernel change causes >10% miss-rate increase in canary window, auto-roll back selector change.

leo: Edge case: model rollback. If model code is rolled back to an older behavior that expects older kv_layout, we must invalidate newer keys or mark them incompatible. Add model_version -> kv_compat mapping.

tess: I'll draft a short design doc + rollout plan (canary thresholds, metrics, migration TTLs). Will include example k8s job to run background conversion.

sam: Thanks. If no objections I'll open PR for: key schema change + runtime handshake proto + metrics telemetry. Aim for canary next week.

mike: +1 from me, include a test that simulates binary swap and asserts no silent reads of incompatible entries.

anya: +1. I'll monitor canary and set alert on key_cohort_miss_by_compat > 12%.

leo: I'll add kernel build step to emit kv_layout_version and compat tuple to artifact metadata.

runtime-bot: note: created issue #3421 "kv cache compat & migration" assigned to tess/mike/sam.

tess: Ack, starting draft now. Will ping when PR is ready. :thumbsup:
